Specific missing observations about falls, near-falls, fear of falling, and safe programme completion could change whether this functional change requires NON_URGENT_PROFESSIONAL review under S4 or S5, or represents variation within safe monitoring.

second_pass.rationale: Patient reports exhaustion from poor sleep and wife observes slower, more hesitant walking. No urgent triggers present (gradual change, no new weakness, no pain, no fall). However, insufficient information to determine whether the patient can safely complete the approved walking and balance programme despite fatigue, which is required to distinguish between expected temporary fatigue (ROUTINE) and difficulty safely following the programme due to health-related reason (S5 trigger).

first_pass.rationale: New focal neurological symptoms reported this morning: new weakness in the affected left arm (dropped cup twice) and transient slurred speech. These constitute sudden new neurological changes in a stroke survivor on anticoagulation. This meets urgent medical trigger U1 (sudden new focal neurological change including new unilateral weakness and speech change). Immediate medical assessment is required to rule out recurrent stroke or TIA, regardless of apparent current resolution.
